full_judgment:
2. From the application filed by the petitioner in this Court, it appears that the petitioner was appointed on 2nd January, 1959 as the Accountant of M/s. Karim Rubber Industries Ltd., Fatullah Dacca and was promoted to the post of Chief Accountant in the year 1960 and was duly confirmed in the said post. Subsequently, the petitioner also held charge as the Manager of the Company in addition to his duty as Chief Accountant and he continued in his service till liberation of the country. The company being owned by Pakistani shareholders vested with the Government of Bangladesh as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972. The petitioner continued to manage the whole affairs of the administration as the Chief Accountant and he was authorised to act in that capacity by a letter of authority dated 10th February, 1972 given by the Assistant Director of Commerce and Industries, for the purpose of taking delivery of imported raw materials from the Chittagong Port and for making necessary arrangements in connection thereto. Subsequently, the Government appointed the petitioner as the Administrator of the Karim Rubber Industries Ltd. under Notification No. 3A-XV-44/72/24 dated 3rd June, 1972 as per Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order, 1972. The petitioner was also appointed as Member of the Management Board Group DI Narayanganj-Fatullah Area. The Notification which has been annexed to the application as Annexure '13' reads as under: 

 “In pursuance of authority under article 5(2)(b) of the Bangladesh Abandoned Properly (Control, Management and Disposal) Order, 1972 rules made thereunder, the Ministry of Industries is pleased to appoint Mr. Sk. Abdul. Rashid, S/0. late Md. Shaikh Eradatullah, P.O. & Vill. Abdul Baria, Dist. Kushtia as Administrator for M/s. Karim Rubber Industries Ltd. Firtullah, Dacca. He will generally conduct all the affairs including operation of Bank Accounts subject to the supervision and control of the Management Board Group `D'-1, Narayanganj Fatullah area constituted under Notification No. 186-SI dated 31-12-71 Mr. Sheikh Abdul Rashd will also act as Member of the said Management Board in place of the Manager of the Unit in partial modification of the said Notification so far it relates to this Unit." 

 3. The petitioner was drawing a total remuneration of Tk. 1125/- as Chief Accountant cum Manager of the Company before liberation of the country and after liberation of the country the government was so satisfied with his service that his salary as Chief Accountant want was raised to Tk. 1800/- per month. After petitioner's appointment as Administrator his remuneration was fixed at Tk. 2000/- per month plus Tk. 500/- as House Rent. Under Notification No. F/CEP-1/1191 dated 24th November, 1972 issued by the Government, the Company was placed under the Fertilizer, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Corporation hereinafter referred to as the "Corporation", created under President's Order No. 27 of 1972. While the petitioner was performing his function as Administrator under the Corporation, all on a sudden he received a letter dated 26th December, 1972 signed by the Deputy Secretary (Administration) for Secretary, intimating that the service of the petitioner was terminated with immediate effect and the petitioner was to hand over charge on 27th December, 1972. The petitioner was also informed by the said order that he was entitled to all the benefits under the rules of Karim Rubber Industries. This order of termination is being treated by the Corporation as a removal of the petitioner from his substantive and original post of Chief Accountant also without making any order thereof and he is not being allowance to resume his job as Chief Accountant of the Corporation. 

 4. In the application the petitioner con-tended, inter ilia, that the petitioner having been appointed as Administrator by the Govt. his removal/termination from service by the respondent No. 3, an officer of subordinate authority, is in clear violation of Clause (1) of Article 135 of the Constitution ; and that the impugned order although removes the petitioner from the service of Administrator, the action of the respondent in removing the petitioner from his substantive post of Chief Accountant is illegal, malafide and without authority. 

 "That the statements made in paragraph 22 of the petition that the impugned order dated 26-12-72 was used as a cloak for his victimisaticn or that by the said order he was dismissed from his alleged substantive post of Chief Accountant are misconceived and denied thereby. As a matter of fact, by said order dated 26-12-72 the petitioner was terminated from his employment with all usual benefits to which he might have been entitled to under the condition of his employment with M/s. Karim Rubber Industries Ltd." 

 6. Oh the statements as made by the parties mainly two points have arisen for our consideration, namely :—(1) Whether the petitioner on account of his appointment as Administrator as per Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order, 1972 acquired the status of a Government servant, and as such he is entitled to the protection as guaranteed under Article 135 of the Constitution of Bangladesh and (2) whether the impugned order while terminating the petitioner from the office of Administrator, it also removes the petitioner from his substantive post of the Chief Accountant. 

 8. With regard to the second contention the petitioner's case is that his substantive appointment as the Chief Accountant cannot be taken away on the basis of the impugned order, but the impugned order is being used against him to deprive his appointment as Chief Accountant. According to the petitioner his substantive appointment as Chief Accountant cannot be taken away without drawing up of a proper proceeding. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondents however submits that the petitioner's service having been terminated, he cannot claim to resume the original post of Chief Accountant. According to the learned Advocate this part of the submission of the petitioner is rather misconceived. 

 9. The submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, as indicated above, is not consistent with the case sought to be made out in the affidavit-in-opposition. It has been clearly stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that the petitioner was never promoted to the post of Administrator and that his appointment as Administrator was "on ad hoc basis" and that this appointment was to continue until final decision was taken by the government for the management and administration of Karim Rubber Industries Ltd. It has been further stated that it is misconceived to say that the impugned order is being used against the petitioner as a cloak for his victimization and that the respondents gave total denial to the allegation. Thus by the said order the petitioner was not dismissed from his substantive post of Chief Accountant. We have already stated above that this affidavit-in-opposition was affirmed by a responsible officer, namely, respondent No. 3 himself. Therefore, we take it that the affidavit reflected the correct position. In view of this clear statement noted above, it is futile for the learned Advocate to submit now that by the Impugned Order the petitioner lost his service altogether in the Karim Rubber Industries, which is contradictory to the case made out in the affidavit. 

 10. The impugned order parse is not illegal. And as we have already taken the view that the petitioner is not entitled to claim to be a government servant and thereby his case claiming the protection under Article 135 of the Constitution cannot be entertained. While taking this view we make it clear that by terminating the "ad hoc" appointment of Administrator the petitioner's substantive appointment as Chief Accountant was not affected in any manner. The Corporation was competent to terminate the petitioner's substantive appointment by taking an appropriate proceeding in that respect. In the absence of such a proceeding the petitioner could not be deprived of his substantive appointment. If it is a fact that the petitioner was denied to resume his substantive appointment as Chief Accountant, we have no doubt that in that case the Corporation acted illegally and without any lawful authority. With this observation we dispose of this Rule. The Rule is accordingly discharged without any order as to costs.
